quote: Wenn die Invarianten einer oder mehrer Formen reell gegeben sind, unter welcher Bedingung gehören dann [-reelle Coefficienten-] Formen dazu, deren Coefficienten reell sind.
english: If the invariants of one or more forms are given as real, under what condition do there then correspond forms whose coefficients are real?
topic: Hilbert asks under what conditions real-valued invariants of forms come from forms with real coefficients, then reflects on logical rigour in mathematics and on judging branches of mathematics by their significance for the development of the human mind, citing Riemann and Cantor.

triage.modern_statement: Let a group G (for example SL_n or GL_n) act on the space V of forms (or systems of forms) of a given type, and let π: V → V//G be the invariant-theoretic quotient map, whose coordinates are the fundamental invariants. Hilbert asks which real points of the quotient (real values of the invariants, satisfying the syzygies) are images of real forms, i.e. points of π(V(ℝ)). If the invariants separate the relevant (closed) orbits, a real point corresponds to a complex orbit that is defined over ℝ. Whether that orbit actually contains a form with real coefficients is a real-descent question, controlled by the Galois cohomology H^1(Gal(ℂ/ℝ), Stab). It is also cut out by semialgebraic conditions (inequalities) on the invariants. The same issue appears in the arithmetic of curves as 'field of moduli vs field of definition': the invariants of a binary form or hyperelliptic curve can be real without the curve being definable over ℝ.
triage.answered_by: There is no single solver, and I found no source showing that anyone answered Hilbert's note specifically. The question was answered in pieces by later work. (a) Equivariant real structures and real forms are handled through Galois cohomology H^1(Gal(ℂ/ℝ), ·); see Adams–Taïbi and work on real structures for reductive group actions. (b) For compact groups, Procesi & Schwarz (Inventiones 81, 1985) gave polynomial inequalities describing the real orbit space. (c) For binary forms and hyperelliptic curves, Shimura and Earle (around 1972) gave the first examples of non-real curves whose field of moduli is ℝ, i.e. real invariants with no real model. Huggins (2005–07 thesis and paper) gave conditions for when a hyperelliptic curve can be defined over its field of moduli (descent holds when Aut(X)/⟨ι⟩ is not cyclic). Later work includes Lercier–Ritzenthaler and others.

evidence.claim: The first examples of closed Riemann surfaces of genus at least two that are not real but have field of moduli ℝ were given by Shimura and Earle around 1972. All of them were hyperelliptic. These are real invariants that come from no real model.
Huggins proved that a hyperelliptic curve descends to its field of moduli if Aut(X)/⟨ι⟩ is not cyclic.
Huggins' thesis studies fields of moduli versus fields of definition of curves. Shimura gave the first examples of curves not definable over their fields of moduli.
Hyperelliptic real curves not definable over their field of moduli are still being studied (Riemann surfaces defined over the reals).
Procesi and Schwarz (Invent. Math. 81, 1985) constructed polynomial inequalities defining the orbit space of a real representation, i.e. which real invariant values actually occur.
Real forms and real structures are classified using the Galois cohomology H^1(Gal(ℂ/ℝ), G).
There is a general criterion for the existence of equivariant real structures on varieties with a reductive group action, using Galois cohomology.

triage.why: Hilbert's question is the real-descent problem for invariants: are real invariant values realized by a real form? It is not among the 23 problems or the 24th problem. The modern answer is general theory (Galois cohomology and real orbit-space inequalities) plus explicit studies for binary forms and hyperelliptic curves. Those studies show that the answer can be no (Shimura and Earle) and give conditions for when it is yes (Huggins and later work). Work on field of moduli vs field of definition, including over ℝ, is still active (papers from 2015–2025). Confidence is medium because Hilbert's note is short and does not say which group, forms or setting he meant. The match to these modern frameworks is my reading of the note; I found no source that discusses this diary entry.
